data.gender_notes: Chitrita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chitrita is a Sanskrit name which means 'Picture or Image'. It is derived from the word 'chitra' which refers to a picture or image. The name Chitrita carries the meaning “Picture or Image” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitrita usually hope their child will grow to embody picture or image and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents the beauty and uniqueness of the divine.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitrita total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chitrita holds significant cultural significance in Hinduism as it reflects the rich artistic heritage of the Indian subcontinent. Art and creativity have long been an integral part of Indian culture, and Chitrita is a reminder of the beauty and power of imagery and visual representation. In Hindu mythology, there are numerous stories and texts that use imagery and symbolism to convey spiritual truths. Therefore, bearing a name that symbolizes an image or picture can evoke a sense of pride and connection to this rich cultural tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Chitrita lies in its symbolic representation of the inner world of the soul. Just as a picture or image can capture and convey complex emotions and ideas, the human soul is said to contain an intricate web of feelings, thoughts, and experiences. By carrying the name Chitrita, one might be reminded of the importance of self-reflection and introspection, as well as the power of visualizing one's inner world in order to gain a deeper understanding of oneself and the world around us. Additionally, in Hindu philosophy, the universe itself is often described as a divine painting or tapestry, and carrying the name Chitrita can serve as a reminder of our connection to the divine creativity and artist within us all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chitrita: Radiant and Creative Mind. In Hindu mythology, Chitri refers to the divine painter who brought the universe into existence through his creative strokes. The name Chitrita symbolizes an individual with a vibrant and imaginative intellect.

historical_references.reference: Chitrita is believed to be the name of a queen who ruled over the Vidarbha region in central India during the 13th century. She is known for her courage and her role in defending the region against the invading forces of the Delhi Sultanate.

Another reference to Chitrita comes from the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata. In this text, Chitrita is the name of a celestial nymph, or apsara, who was the wife of the god Indra. She is described as a beautiful and graceful being who lived in the heavenly realm.
